result.detailed_feedback:
**Element Layout (19.0 points):**
The video utilizes a highly effective split-screen layout that separates conceptual text (left) from dynamic visual proofs and animations (right). This spatial organization respects the learner's cognitive load by allowing them to read the premise before observing the mathematical manifestation. The use of whitespace is excellent, preventing the screen from feeling cluttered even when complex graphs and formulas are presented simultaneously. The visual hierarchy is clear, with bold headers and highlighted boxes for key formulas like F'(x)=f(x).

**Attractiveness (18.5 points):**
The aesthetic is professional and reminiscent of high-end educational channels like 3Blue1Brown. The dark background provides a high-contrast canvas for the vibrant green and orange plot lines, which helps in maintaining focus. The animations—particularly the 'scrubber' effect showing the area accumulation in real-time—are smooth and visually stimulating. The creative use of the 'Undo Button' metaphor adds a layer of relatability to an abstract concept.

**Logic Flow (20.0 points):**
The pedagogical scaffolding is nearly perfect. It begins with a relatable physical context (position vs. speed), transitions into the formal definition of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC), provides a visual intuition through the 'Area Function' accumulation, and concludes with a practical application and a high-level summary. The transition from the visual slope of the area function to the height of the original function is the logical 'aha!' moment that is executed flawlessly here.

**Accuracy & Depth (20.0 points):**
The content is mathematically rigorous and factually accurate. It correctly identifies the two parts of the FTC: the derivative of an integral and the evaluation of a definite integral via antiderivatives. The depth is appropriate for an introductory calculus student, moving beyond rote memorization to explain *why* the inverse relationship exists. The example using v(t)=2t to find distance is a classic and effective choice to ground the theory in reality.

**Visual Consistency (19.0 points):**
There is a strong sense of visual cohesion throughout the video. The color palette is consistent (green for the function/area, yellow for text highlights), and the typography remains uniform. The transition between static text slides and animated graphing sequences is seamless, maintaining a professional standard that doesn't distract the learner with jarring style shifts.

**Overall Summary:**
This is an exceptional educational video that masterfully explains the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. By balancing formal mathematical notation with intuitive visual animations, it effectively bridges the gap between 'doing' calculus and 'understanding' calculus. The pedagogical approach is highly suitable for the subject matter, particularly in how it illustrates integration as an accumulation process that is the direct inverse of differentiation.

**Key Strengths:**
• Excellent visual representation of the Area Function A(x) growing in real-time.
• Clear, logical progression from physical intuition to formal theorem.
• High-contrast, professional visual design that reduces cognitive load.
• Effective use of the 'Undo' metaphor to explain inverse operations.
• Precise mathematical notation and accurate terminology.

**Areas for Improvement:**
• The initial 'Zippy' introduction could feature a small icon or simplified animation of the runner to increase engagement for younger audiences.
• A brief mention of the 'constant of integration' (C) during the antiderivative shortcut section might prevent common student errors, though it is often omitted in basic FTC introductions.
• Slightly increasing the font size of the axis labels on the graphs would improve readability on smaller mobile screens.
